question.problem:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence:

$$
{a}_{n+1}={a}_{n}-8,\,\,{a}_{1}=2,\,\,n\ge 1
$$

The explicit formula for the $n$th term is

${a}_{n}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,n\ge 1.$
question.worked_solution:
The explicit formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}+(n-1)d,\,n\ge 1,
$$

so we need to determine the first term ${a}_{1}$ and the common difference $d.$

We are given that the first term is ${a}_{1}=2,$ and we can use the recursive rule to compute the second term, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={a}_{1}-8 \\  & =2-8 \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Using the first and second terms, we can compute the common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & ={a}_{2}-{a}_{1} \\  & =-6-2 \\  & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute ${a}_{1}=2$ and $d=-8$ into the formula for the $n$th term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\  & =2+(n-1)(-8) \\  & =2-8n+8 \\  & =10-8n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=10-8n,\,n\ge 1.
$$
